Will an Anker SOLIX Solarbank 3 E2700 Pro run an electric kettle? (EU)

Exceeds output — nothing to time — it will not run see why below ↓

The load is more than this inverter can sustain. 3,000 W against 1,200 W continuous — 250% of it. No accessory closes a gap that size — it takes a bigger inverter.

Official spec + Derived by WattPair · verified 2026-08-01 · EU unit × electric kettle

Nominal capacity 2,688 Wh
Surge headroom 0.4×
The machine that does run it

EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 (EU 230 V) — 4,000 W continuous · from €3,299. See that pairing →

Running3,000 Wnot nameplateof1,200 Wcontinuous output

0 – 3,000 W across the rails above. The figure above is not this load’s nameplate rating, printed separately below.

No start-up rail: this load has no locked rotor to publish an inrush for, so no start-up demand was checked.

Two numbers decide this, and readers use them interchangeably: watts are the ceiling on what the inverter holds at any instant, watt-hours are how much energy the battery holds. A machine can have plenty of one and not enough of the other.

The verdict is a calculation, not a lookup. What it will not do is print a runtime, and the reason is specific: there is nothing to time. A runtime for a load this machine will not start is a figure about nothing.

Where those numbers come from

A blank is never left blank. A field we have found no figure for says so, and a field whose sources disagree — two documents, or one document with itself — says that instead of picking one.

No usable-capacity figure for this machine

Anker SOLIX states a nameplate watt-hour number for it, and we have found no published depth of discharge or inverter efficiency for the EU build. Dividing the nameplate by this load would be wrong by 20–35% in the flattering direction, so this page shows the nameplate for what it is and refuses to turn it into hours.

Missing: station.usable_capacity_wh

The surge ceiling on this page is ours, not the manufacturer’s

We have found no published surge rating for the EU build. So the start-up check runs against the continuous output instead — an inverter cannot surge below what it sustains, which makes that the safest number we can defend. Real inverters usually manage 1.5–2× their continuous rating, so a start-up call held back by this figure may well be fine in practice; we are not going to say so until the manufacturer does.

Energy rate instead of a runtime

3,000 Wh per hour averaged over this load’s duty cycle

This number needs no battery figure at all, which is why this page can give it when it cannot give hours. Divide any usable-capacity figure you trust by it and you have your own runtime, with our arithmetic visible instead of hidden.

Questions people ask about this pairing

Will an Anker SOLIX Solarbank 3 E2700 Pro run an electric kettle?
No. The binding constraint is the continuous output: 3,000 W against 1,200 W continuous. That is a calculation against this machine's own record, not a lookup, and the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 is the machine in our library that does clear it.
How long will an Anker SOLIX Solarbank 3 E2700 Pro run an electric kettle?
It does not, so there are no hours to give. That is why the panel at the top shows an em dash rather than a number: a runtime for a load the machine cannot start is a figure about nothing.
Where does the surge ceiling for the Anker SOLIX Solarbank 3 E2700 Pro come from?
From us, and the page says so every time it uses it. We have found no published surge rating for the EU build. So the start-up check runs against the continuous output as a conservative floor — an inverter cannot surge below what it sustains. Real inverters usually manage 1.5–2× their continuous rating, which means a start-up call held back by this figure may well be fine in practice. We will not say so until the manufacturer publishes a number.
